title: The Future of Research Infrastructure

sourceEvidence.locator: 1.1 The shift from output generation to research control
sourceEvidence.excerpt: The book proposes a research control plane: a persistent environment in which scientific questions, claims, evidence, experiments, decisions, agents, tools, and human authority remain connected over time. The need for such an environment appears as soon as AI can generate more plausible scientific work than a team can verify, understand, and integrate. The scarce resource moves from production to judgment.

sourceEvidence.locator: 1.1 The shift from output generation to research control
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Imagine a laboratory or research company five years from now, although much of the scenario is already technically possible. A principal investigator begins the morning with an unresolved question. Before lunch, a literature agent has searched several corpora, a planning agent has proposed four experimental branches, a coding agent has implemented two analyses, a reproduction agent has rerun an older result, and an AI reviewer has identified a statistical weakness in one branch. In parallel, colleagues have discussed the project in a meeting, changed an assumption, and decided that one attractive direction is too expensive to pursue. The organisation has produced more work in a few hours than a small team could once produce in weeks.

sourceEvidence.locator: 1.1 The shift from output generation to research control
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Nothing in that picture guarantees scientific progress. The team may now have ten times more artefacts and less clarity about what it actually knows. Two agents may have used different versions of the dataset. A generated experiment may have been designed to optimise a convenient proxy instead of the scientific question. A literature search may have missed a crucial vocabulary. A negative result may be buried in an execution log while the polished report preserves only successful runs. A meeting may have changed the meaning of the project without updating the plan that agents continue to execute. If one model is replaced next month, its conversational memory may disappear and with it the rationale that held the work together.

sourceEvidence.locator: 1.1 The shift from output generation to research control
sourceEvidence.excerpt: The problem is not a lack of intelligence in the individual tools. It is the absence of an infrastructure that makes scientific meaning persistent while intelligence is distributed. Contemporary AI products are usually organised around an inference: assemble context, send a request to a model, receive an answer. Scientific projects are organised around a history: a question changes, evidence accumulates, methods fail, interpretations branch, decisions are revised, and responsibility shifts among people and institutions. A research organisation therefore needs an object that survives every individual model call. That object is the project itself, represented as an explicit and versioned scientific state.

hook: A laboratory produces a week's worth of work before lunch, then loses track of what it knows.
readerPromise: Understand the proposed infrastructure needed to preserve scientific meaning across distributed AI-assisted work.
protectedRevelations: Detailed control-plane architecture, transaction procedures and deployment prescriptions.
